```{r panel-description, echo=FALSE}
description <- "
Panel J: Male-inhibited and male-excited mAL subtypes target different P1 neurons
==================================================================================
mAL subtypes split by their ppk23 (male contact) response polarity show distinct
patterns of downstream connectivity to P1 courtship command neurons, using
input-normalized synaptic weights (fraction of each P1 neuron's total input).

Top:    Heatmap of signed input-normalized mAL -> P1 weights, rows annotated by
```

## Assign ppk23 response groups

```{r ppk23-groups}
# Split mAL subtypes by ppk23 response polarity (male encounter)
ppk23_response <- mal_activation_matrix[mal_subtypes, "ppk23"]
ppk23_group <- ifelse(ppk23_response < 0, "ppk23-inhibited", "ppk23-excited")

ppk23_group_colors <- c(
  "ppk23-inhibited" = "#E41A1C",
  "ppk23-excited"   = "#377EB8"
)

cat("ppk23 response groups:\n")
for (g in c("ppk23-inhibited", "ppk23-excited")) {
  members <- names(ppk23_group[ppk23_group == g])
  cat(sprintf("  %s (%d): %s\n", g, length(members), paste(members, collapse = ", ")))
}
```

## Extract input-normalized mAL -> P1 connectivity

```{r mal-p1-normed}
# adj.matrix is post-normalized (input-normalized): adj.matrix[pre, post]
# Values = fraction of postsynaptic neuron's total input from presynaptic type
mal_p1_normed <- matrix(0, nrow = length(mal_subtypes), ncol = length(p1_subtypes),
                        dimnames = list(mal_subtypes, p1_subtypes))

# Extract from sparse matrix (check that types exist as dimnames)
adj_rows <- rownames(adj.matrix)
adj_cols <- colnames(adj.matrix)

for (mal in mal_subtypes) {
  for (p1 in p1_subtypes) {
    if (mal %in% adj_rows && p1 %in% adj_cols) {
      mal_p1_normed[mal, p1] <- adj.matrix[mal, p1]
    }
  }
}

cat("Input-normalized mAL -> P1 matrix (fraction of P1 input):\n")
print(round(mal_p1_normed, 6))

# Apply NT signs: GABAergic mAL output is inhibitory
mal_p1_signed <- mal_p1_normed
for (mal in rownames(mal_p1_signed)) {
  nt <- mal_nt[mal]
  if (!is.na(nt) && nt == "GABA") {
    mal_p1_signed[mal, ] <- -abs(mal_p1_signed[mal, ])
  }
}

cat("\nSigned input-normalized mAL -> P1 matrix:\n")
print(round(mal_p1_signed, 6))
```

## Heatmap: mAL -> P1 by ppk23 group

```{r heatmap, fig.width=12, fig.height=12}
# Order rows: ppk23-inhibited first (sorted by ppk23 strength), then ppk23-excited
row_order <- order(ppk23_group[mal_subtypes], ppk23_response[mal_subtypes])
mat_ordered <- mal_p1_signed[mal_subtypes[row_order], ]

# Row annotations
row_annot <- data.frame(
  ppk23_group      = ppk23_group[rownames(mat_ordered)],
  neurotransmitter = mal_nt[rownames(mat_ordered)],
  row.names        = rownames(mat_ordered)
)

ann_colors <- list(
  ppk23_group      = ppk23_group_colors,
  neurotransmitter = nt_colors
)

# Diverging palette
max_abs <- max(abs(mat_ordered))
if (max_abs == 0) max_abs <- 1
breaks <- seq(-max_abs, max_abs, length.out = 101)
colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "#4393C3", "#92C5DE", "#D1E5F0",
                              "white",
                              "#FDDBC7", "#F4A582", "#D6604D", "#B2182B"))(100)

# Find gap position between groups
n_inhibited <- sum(ppk23_group[rownames(mat_ordered)] == "ppk23-inhibited")

# Dynamic cell sizing
n_p1 <- ncol(mat_ordered)
n_mal <- nrow(mat_ordered)
cw <- min(40, max(15, 400 / n_p1))
ch <- min(20, max(10, 500 / n_mal))
fig_w <- max(10, n_p1 * cw / 72 + 4)
fig_h <- max(10, n_mal * ch / 72 + 3)

save_heatmap_fixed_annot(
  mat        = mat_ordered,
  row_annot  = row_annot,
  col_annot  = data.frame(row.names = colnames(mat_ordered)),
  ann_colors = ann_colors,
  filename   = file.path(panel_plot_dir("panel_J_heatmap", "png"),
                         "panel_J_heatmap.png"),
  width      = fig_w, height = fig_h,
  breaks     = breaks, color = colors,
  cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = TRUE,
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  fontsize_row = 6, fontsize_col = 8,
  border_color = "grey90",
  cellwidth = cw, cellheight = ch,
  gaps_row = n_inhibited
)

save_heatmap_fixed_annot(
  mat        = mat_ordered,
  row_annot  = row_annot,
  col_annot  = data.frame(row.names = colnames(mat_ordered)),
  ann_colors = ann_colors,
  filename   = file.path(panel_plot_dir("panel_J_heatmap", "pdf"),
                         "panel_J_heatmap.pdf"),
  width      = fig_w, height = fig_h,
  breaks     = breaks, color = colors,
  cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = TRUE,
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  fontsize_row = 6, fontsize_col = 8,
  border_color = "grey90",
  cellwidth = cw, cellheight = ch,
  gaps_row = n_inhibited
)
```

## Grouped box plot: total P1 output by ppk23 group

```{r boxplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
# Total signed output to all P1 subtypes per mAL subtype
total_p1 <- data.frame(
  mAL_subtype = mal_subtypes,
  total_p1_output = rowSums(abs(mal_p1_normed)),
  total_p1_signed = rowSums(mal_p1_signed),
  ppk23_group = ppk23_group[mal_subtypes],
  ppk23_strength = ppk23_response[mal_subtypes],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

p_box <- ggplot(total_p1, aes(x = ppk23_group, y = total_p1_output, fill = ppk23_group)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ppk23_group_colors) +
  labs(x = "ppk23 response group",
       y = "Total input-normalized P1 output\n(sum of |input fractions|)",
       fill = "ppk23 group") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

save_fig5_plot(p_box, "panel_J_boxplot", width = 7, height = 6)
print(p_box)
```

## Statistical test

```{r stats}
if (length(unique(total_p1$ppk23_group)) > 1) {
  test_total <- wilcox.test(total_p1_output ~ ppk23_group, data = total_p1)
  test_signed <- wilcox.test(total_p1_signed ~ ppk23_group, data = total_p1)
  cat("Wilcoxon test - total |P1 output|: p =", format(test_total$p.value, digits = 3), "\n")
  cat("Wilcoxon test - signed P1 output:  p =", format(test_signed$p.value, digits = 3), "\n")
} else {
  cat("Only one ppk23 group present -- skipping test\n")
  test_total <- list(p.value = NA)
  test_signed <- list(p.value = NA)
}
```

## Per-P1 bar chart: predicted drive under encounter scenarios

```{r per-p1-bars, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
# Define 3 encounter scenarios (same as Panel F)
# Lone male encounter excluded: male contact always co-occurs with cVA
scenarios <- c(
  "Female (ppk25)" = "ppk25",
  "cVA + male (cVA+ppk23)"      = "DA1+ppk23",
  "cVA + female (cVA+ppk25)"    = "DA1+ppk25"
)

scenario_colors <- c(
  "Female (ppk25)" = "#D73027",
  "cVA + male (cVA+ppk23)"      = "#8E24AA",
  "cVA + female (cVA+ppk25)"    = "#F57C00"
)

# Build mAL population response per scenario (from activation matrix)
scenario_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = length(scenarios), ncol = length(mal_subtypes),
                       dimnames = list(names(scenarios), mal_subtypes))
for (i in seq_along(scenarios)) {
  channels <- strsplit(scenarios[i], "\\+")[[1]]
  for (ch in channels) {
    if (ch %in% colnames(mal_activation_matrix)) {
      scenario_mat[i, ] <- scenario_mat[i, ] + mal_activation_matrix[mal_subtypes, ch]
    }
  }
}

# For each P1 subtype and scenario, compute predicted drive:
# drive = sum over mAL of (mAL response) * (mAL -> P1 signed weight)
per_p1 <- data.frame()
for (p1 in p1_subtypes) {
  for (sc in names(scenarios)) {
    drive <- sum(scenario_mat[sc, ] * mal_p1_signed[, p1])
    per_p1 <- rbind(per_p1, data.frame(
      P1 = p1, scenario = sc,
      predicted_drive = drive,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
  }
}
per_p1$scenario <- factor(per_p1$scenario, levels = names(scenarios))

# Order P1 subtypes by male encounter drive
p1_order <- per_p1 %>%
  filter(scenario == "cVA + male (cVA+ppk23)") %>%
  arrange(predicted_drive) %>%
  pull(P1)
per_p1$P1 <- factor(per_p1$P1, levels = p1_order)

p_per_p1 <- ggplot(per_p1, aes(x = P1, y = predicted_drive, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = scenario_colors) +
  labs(x = "P1 subtype",
       y = "Predicted mAL drive on P1\n(scenario activation x signed input fraction)",
       fill = "Encounter scenario") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_per_p1, "panel_J_per_p1_bars", width = 12, height = 6)
print(p_per_p1)
```

## Continuous analysis: ppk23 strength vs P1 output

```{r continuous-scatter, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
# Instead of just binary split, show the continuous relationship
p_continuous <- ggplot(total_p1, aes(x = ppk23_strength, y = total_p1_output)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = ppk23_group), size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey40",
              linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("ppk23-inhibited" = 16, "ppk23-excited" = 17),
                     name = "ppk23 group") +
  labs(x = "ppk23 net path strength",
       y = "Total P1 input fraction\n(sum of |input fractions|)") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

# Spearman correlation
if (nrow(total_p1) > 3) {
  cor_ppk23_p1 <- cor.test(total_p1$ppk23_strength, total_p1$total_p1_output,
                            method = "spearman")
  cat(sprintf("Spearman correlation (ppk23 strength vs P1 output): rho=%.3f, p=%.4f\n",
              cor_ppk23_p1$estimate, cor_ppk23_p1$p.value))
} else {
  cor_ppk23_p1 <- list(estimate = NA, p.value = NA)
}

save_fig5_plot(p_continuous, "panel_J_continuous_scatter", width = 8, height = 6)
print(p_continuous)
```

## Panel narrative

```{r narrative, echo=FALSE}
n_inhibited <- sum(ppk23_group == "ppk23-inhibited")
n_excited <- sum(ppk23_group == "ppk23-excited")
mean_p1_inh <- mean(total_p1$total_p1_output[total_p1$ppk23_group == "ppk23-inhibited"])
mean_p1_exc <- mean(total_p1$total_p1_output[total_p1$ppk23_group == "ppk23-excited"])
fold_diff <- ifelse(mean_p1_exc > 0, mean_p1_inh / mean_p1_exc, Inf)

# Continuous correlation text
cor_text <- if (!is.na(cor_ppk23_p1$estimate)) {
  sprintf("rho=%.3f, p=%s", cor_ppk23_p1$estimate,
          format(cor_ppk23_p1$p.value, digits = 3))
} else {
  "not computed"
}

# Which P1 subtypes get more input from each group
p1_bias <- sapply(p1_subtypes, function(p1) {
  inh_members <- names(ppk23_group[ppk23_group == "ppk23-inhibited"])
  exc_members <- names(ppk23_group[ppk23_group == "ppk23-excited"])
  inh_total <- sum(mal_p1_normed[inh_members, p1])
  exc_total <- sum(mal_p1_normed[exc_members, p1])
  ifelse(inh_total > exc_total, "ppk23-inhibited", "ppk23-excited")
})

p_text <- format(test_total$p.value, digits = 3)

narrative <- sprintf(
"PANEL J: ppk23 Response Group vs P1 Connectivity
===================================================

WHAT THIS PANEL SHOWS
---------------------
mAL subtypes are split into two groups based on their response to ppk23
(male contact): ppk23-inhibited (%d subtypes, net negative path strength)
and ppk23-excited (%d subtypes, net positive). This panel asks: do these
two groups connect differently to downstream P1 courtship command neurons?

Connectivity is measured as INPUT-NORMALIZED synaptic weights -- the fraction
of each P1 neuron's total input that comes from each mAL subtype. This
controls for differences in P1 neuron size and total synapse count.

Top: Heatmap of signed input-normalized mAL -> P1 weights, with rows split
by ppk23 response group and annotated by NT.

Middle: Box plot comparing total P1 output between the two groups.

Bottom: Per-P1 bar chart showing the total input fraction from each group.

KEY OBSERVATIONS
----------------
1. ppk23-inhibited subtypes have mean total P1 output = %.6f;
   ppk23-excited subtypes = %.6f (%.1fx difference).
   Wilcoxon p = %s.

2. Continuous relationship (ppk23 strength vs P1 output): %s.

3. P1 subtype bias: %s

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
-------------------------
If ppk23-inhibited subtypes (which are suppressed during male contact)
connect more strongly to P1, this creates a disinhibition mechanism:
male pheromones suppress these mAL subtypes, releasing P1 from their
inhibitory drive. Conversely, ppk23-excited subtypes (activated during
male contact) would INCREASE P1 inhibition during male encounters.

The differential targeting of P1 subtypes by the two groups means that
male vs female contact could selectively release different P1 command
neurons from inhibition, enabling sex-specific courtship responses.

PLACE IN THE FIGURE 5 STORY
----------------------------
Panel J connects the ppk23 sign reversal (Panel C) to the P1 output
specificity (Panel D). While Panel C showed that subtypes differ in
ppk23 polarity and Panel D showed they target different P1 neurons,
Panel J tests whether these two properties are CORRELATED -- whether
the subtypes that are inhibited by male contact are the same ones that
project most heavily to specific P1 command neurons.
",
n_inhibited, n_excited,
mean_p1_inh, mean_p1_exc, fold_diff, p_text,
cor_text,
paste(sprintf("  %s: biased toward %s", p1_subtypes, p1_bias), collapse = "\n")
)

save_panel_narrative("panel_J", narrative)
cat(narrative)
```
